All done. Here's the final result:

**Correctness**: 5/5 trials pass.  
**Performance**: 6.56ms (mean) vs 5.66ms reference — about 1.16x slower, well within reach.

The implementation uses a single fused AveLang kernel that does Conv2d (16→64 channels, 3×3), channel-min reduction, and tanh×2 epilogue in one pass. The critical optimization was loading the 3×3×16 input patch into local registers once and reusing it across all 64 output channels — this alone dropped runtime from ~17ms to 6.6ms. All 9216 conv weights are cooperatively staged into shared memory once per block.

The fused approach avoids the reference's intermediate (128, 64, 254, 254) tensor (~528M elements / ~1GB) entirely, computing everything in registers and writing only the final (128, 1, 254, 254) output.
